clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's return to the family in 1989 and through 1994: your sleep began to shift, you dropped chess and debate, settled into a rebuilt house with your mother and stepfather, leaned hard on your friend Rafe at conservatory, hurt your wrist and stopped playing, lost footing after his death in 1991 and your mother's remarriage, drifted at community college, then recovered when you found your drive again abroad. Your grandmother Gordon had thyroid surgery within a year or so of his death in 1991. Shifts in your functioning and symptoms pile up across these years, with your own recovery and your grandmother's health marking the span.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002 and her death in February 2004: you ran out of steam for performing, faced a disastrous audition, grew distant from family and friends, left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol, split from her, sank into depression through the winter of 2003, and relied on friends while unable to face your parents. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home. Shifts in your functioning, anxiety and relationships reach from the diagnosis through your settling into recovery by early 2004.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008 and your grandfather Clifford's death around the same time: you built with Silas at Alder Creek, grew too drained for conversation with your mother, she pressed to visit against your wishes and the visit went wrong, you kept the door shut on her, then stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school in August. Two shifts in your distance from your mother sit around the lodge visit in late July, a few weeks before you moved away, held together by how little talking happened and how tense contact became.

clusters.name: Wren's marriage and her family's closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and into late 2019: your contact with your mother eased off slightly, your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, your sister Tara married and began her first pregnancy, Leo returned nearby with his family, your job steadied but you felt you ought to drive projects forward, you started a sleeping pill, aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother, and at the lake house for Frances's retirement in October 2019, Wren grew swamped and you overfunctioned to settle her, she stays fused with her father and brother, you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as others rose, and Wren grew anxious when you had not slept at family occasions. Shifts in your anxiety, your mother's distance, and your functioning span nearly three years and cluster around Wren's family, her mother's retirement gathering and the pattern of your sleep at those occasions.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
